title: ACH and the NACHA File Format

questions.question: A fixed-width record holds an amount in a 10-character numeric field of US cents. How is 1,234.56 USD written?
options: 0001234.56, keeping the decimal point so the reader knows the scale
0000123456, right-justified and zero-filled as an integer of cents
123456    , left-justified and space-filled like the name fields
1234560000, left-justified and zero-filled to the field's full width
questions.explanation: Amounts are integer minor units, and Nacha numeric fields are right-justified and zero-filled, so 123456 cents becomes 0000123456. Left-justifying is the strongest distractor because alphameric fields work that way, but a reader that parses the field as a number would see 1234560000 cents or reject the spaces.

questions.question: A batch has three entries to receiving DFIs 011999993, 061999998, and 121999993 (check digits included). What entry hash goes in the Batch Control?
options: 0195999984, the sum of the full nine-digit routing numbers
0000000003, the count of entries in the batch, zero-filled
Each prefix's check digit summed, then zero-filled to ten digits
0019599997, the sum of the eight-digit prefixes, zero-filled
questions.explanation: The entry hash sums the eight-digit receiving DFI identification of each entry, excluding the check digit, and keeps the rightmost ten digits: 01199999 + 06199999 + 12199999 = 19599997. Summing the full nine-digit numbers is the common mistake; the receiver would compute a different hash and reject the batch.

questions.question: A subscription business debits a consumer's checking account under an authorization captured on its website. Which SEC code and transaction code apply?
options: WEB in the Batch Header and 27 on each Entry Detail record
PPD in the Batch Header and 22 on each Entry Detail record
CCD in the Batch Header and 27 on each Entry Detail record
WEB in the Batch Header and 37 on each Entry Detail record
questions.explanation: The SEC code says how the debit was authorized (WEB: online, consumer) and the transaction code says account type and direction (27: checking debit). 37 is the closest distractor, but it debits a savings account; PPD with 22 would be a consumer credit, and CCD is for business receivers.

questions.question: An entry settles on Thursday 2026-10-15. What is the last date an RDFI may return it with R01, Insufficient Funds?
options: Saturday 2026-10-17, two calendar days after the settlement date
Friday 2026-10-16, one banking day after the settlement date
Monday 2026-10-19, two banking days after the settlement date
Monday 2026-12-14, sixty calendar days after the settlement date
questions.explanation: R01 is an operational return with a two-banking-day window: Friday is day one, the weekend is skipped, and Monday the 19th is day two. The sixty-calendar-day window applies to unauthorized-debit returns such as R10, which is why a business that treats settlement as final keeps receiving returns for weeks.

questions.question: Why does the entry hash sum receiving routing numbers when the Batch Control already carries total debits and total credits?
options: It is a cryptographic checksum that proves the file was not tampered with
It lets the ACH Operator sort entries to the receiving banks more quickly
It catches an entry sent to the wrong bank even when its amount is right
It replaces the trace number as the key for matching returns to entries
questions.explanation: Amount errors are already caught by the debit and credit totals; the entry hash covers a different field, so a shifted or altered routing number changes a declared total. It is not cryptographic: anyone can recompute it, and the format's authentication comes from the transport and the ODFI agreement, not from the file.

questions.question: Debits come back with R01, R02, R09, and R10. Which of them may the Originator re-present?
options: All four, as long as each is retried within two banking days
R01 and R10, because the customer can fund or approve the debit later
Only R02, after the customer provides a replacement account number
R01 and R09, at most twice more within 180 days, marked RETRY PYMT
questions.explanation: Only insufficient and uncollected funds may be re-presented, up to two more times within 180 days of the original settlement, with the description RETRY PYMT. R10 is the dangerous distractor: it means the customer says the debit was not authorized, so retrying it is a new unauthorized debit that counts toward the 0.5 percent threshold.
